standfirst: Spumaretrovirinae is a subfamily rather than a genus, holding five foamy virus genera together. It is the most feature-rich of the four retroviral modules: the structural trio plus two bel regulators, plus Bet, a spliced protein the deposited vocabulary names but no profile can represent.

modules.Spumaretrovirinae: Bet is Bel-1 (Tas) residues 1–88 spliced to the last 396 residues of Bel-2 — one intron in the coding sequence, which is what brings it within reach of the splice caller. Its 30 deposits sat unmodelled because a protein assembled from two genes is not collinear with any genomic ORF, so a profile built from it would be trained to find something the genome does not contain.

gaps: BET's rate is bounded by reference coverage, and every gap in it is accounted for. Bovispumavirus and Equispumavirus have no reference because neither has a genuine Bet deposit — the curated bovine records map contiguously onto the called BEL2 at 97.9% identity, so they are Bel-2. Taxon 11963 contributes none of its nineteen genomes because eighteen have zero tblastn hits against a 482 aa Bet: they are 10.0–12.5 kb gag-pol-env deposits carrying no bel region at all. The remaining misses are genomes that fail to call TAS or BEL2, and Bet needs both of its parent exons. TAS and BEL2 themselves have a residual recall gap that is NOT a cutoff problem — the regions score 197–578 bits against cutoffs of 19 and 50 — and remains open.
